speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing acute diarrhea; to help me determine the cause, how long has this been going on and what does your stool look like?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea (likely Clostridioides difficile infection). Given the history of recent levofloxacin use for pneumonia, the high frequency of watery stools (9 episodes in 2 days), and abdominal cramping, this is a classic presentation of *C. difficile* colitis. I am requesting the results of a C. difficile toxin assay. REQUEST TEST: C.diff_toxin_assay
